import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1176

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1176](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1176)
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Erdos1176

/--
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

A problem of Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal. The consistency of this was proved by Hajnal and Komjáth.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_1176 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = aleph 1 →
      ∃ (EColor : Type) (_ : mk EColor = aleph 1) (c_edge : G.edgeSet → EColor),
        ∀ (VColor : Type) (_ : mk VColor ≤ aleph 0) (c_vert : V → VColor),
          ∃ (vc : VColor),
            ∀ (ec : EColor), ∃ (u v : V) (h : G.Adj u v),
              c_vert u = vc ∧ c_vert v = vc ∧ c_edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩ = ec := by
  sorry

end Erdos1176

reformulations.difference: The colouring conclusion chooses an arbitrary edge-colour type of cardinality ℵ₁ without explicitly requiring surjectivity, and quantifies over all vertex-colour types of cardinality at most ℵ₀. This is equivalent to using a fixed ℵ₁-sized edge palette, requiring every edge colour to occur, and testing all maps V → ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any two ℵ₁-sized palettes are bijective, so edge colours can be relabelled. Applying the stated property to the constant vertex colouring into Unit forces c_edge to be surjective. Every at-most-countable vertex palette embeds into ℕ, preserving its colour classes. Because the edge palette is nonempty, a class containing every edge colour contains vertices and therefore corresponds to an actual colour in the original palette. Conversely, ℕ is one of the allowed countable palettes. The theorem palette_encoding_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this equivalence for every graph.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the sole declaration. The source's status, “NOT DISPROVABLE — Open in general,” is compatible with research open; the stated consistency result does not settle the general question. Scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings. They prove that chromaticCardinal is an attained minimum, that complete graphs have chromatic cardinal equal to their vertex cardinality, that the ℵ₁ hypothesis is satisfiable and excludes countable graphs, and that the endpoint predicate means precisely that one vertex-colour class contains an edge of every colour. Finite tests also confirmed unordered-edge symmetry, loop exclusion, and colour-class behaviour. The checked proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The reviewed file was not modified.
